related_questions.question: What is a simple definition of credit score?

text_blocks.snippet: A credit score is a three-digit number, typically between 300 and 850, that represents how likely someone is to repay borrowed money. It's a snapshot of a person's creditworthiness, based on their credit history, and is used by lenders to assess the risk of lending money.

list.title: What it is:
list.snippet: A credit score is a numerical representation of a person's credit history, compiled from information in their credit report.

list.title: How it's used:
list.snippet: Lenders, like banks and credit card companies, use credit scores to determine whether to approve loan or credit card applications and to set interest rates.

list.title: What it reflects:
list.snippet: A higher credit score generally indicates that a person is more responsible with borrowing and repaying debt, while a lower score suggests a higher risk for lenders.

list.title: Factors influencing the score:
list.snippet: Key factors include payment history, amounts owed, length of credit history, types of credit used, and recent credit inquiries.

list.title: Common scoring models:
list.snippet: The most widely used credit scoring models are FICO and VantageScore, according to City National Bank.

list.title: Score ranges:
list.snippet: FICO scores typically range from 300 to 850, while VantageScore ranges from 300 to 850 (or 501 to 990).

list.title: Importance:
list.snippet: A good credit score can lead to better loan terms, lower interest rates, and easier access to credit, while a poor score can result in higher interest rates, fewer credit options, and even rejection of applications.

related_questions.question: What credit score does an 18 year old start with?

text_blocks.snippet: An 18-year-old typically starts with no credit score or a blank slate when it comes to credit. Credit scores are generated by credit bureaus based on your credit history, which builds up over time as you use credit products like credit cards or loans. It usually takes a few months (around 3-6 months) after opening your first credit account for a credit score to be generated.

list.title: No inherent score at 18:
list.snippet: Turning 18 doesn't automatically assign you a credit score.

list.title: Building credit:
list.snippet: You need to actively start using credit to build a credit history and, consequently, a credit score.

list.title: Starting with a blank slate:
list.snippet: Without a credit history, you'll have a "thin file" or no credit score at all.

list.title: How credit scores are built:
list.snippet: Credit scores are calculated based on factors like your payment history, credit utilization (how much of your available credit you're using), length of credit history, and types of credit used.

list.title: Average score for 18-year-olds:
list.snippet: While there's no starting score, SoFi reports that the average FICO score for 18-year-olds is around 681, according to American Express. This is considered a "good" score, but it's based on those who have already started building credit, not a starting point.
